That sounds exhausting, especially if it's been dragging on for months. Before you do anything tomorrow, can we talk it through tonight? Quitting might genuinely be the right call, but I want to make sure it's a decision and not just a reaction to a bad week. Do you have anything lined up, or would this be a leap without a net? Either way I've got you, I just want you to walk into it with clear eyes.

## 2

I get why the space photos feel like the weak point to poke at, since most of us will never see Earth with our own eyes. But the roundness isn't resting on NASA's word alone. Sailors noticed ships disappearing hull-first over the horizon centuries before spaceflight. Eratosthenes measured Earth's curvature using shadows around 240 BC, no satellites involved. Flights from Sydney to Santiago take routes that only make sense on a sphere. And it's not just one country's space agency: Russia, China, India, Japan, and the European Space Agency have all independently sent up craft and gotten images consistent with a globe. For the photos to be fake, you'd need every one of these unconnected groups, across decades, coordinating a lie with zero credible leaks. What specifically convinced you the photos were staged?

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it's actually every color mixed together, like a secret rainbow hiding in plain light. When that light hits our atmosphere, it crashes into tiny molecules of gas, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. Here's the trick: blue light has shorter, choppier waves than red light, and shorter waves bounce off those molecules much more easily. So blue light gets scattered all over the sky, bouncing from molecule to molecule, while red and orange light mostly just plow straight through. Wherever you look up, some of that bounced blue light is heading toward your eyes. That's why the sky glows blue instead of staying colorless. At sunset, you're looking through much more air sideways, so even the blue gets scattered away and only the red and orange survive the trip to your eyes.

## 4

雨落在深夜的街道上，路灯的光被打湿，散成一片朦胧的黄晕。雨声敲打着窗户，像是谁在轻轻叩门，又没有人回应。远处偶尔驶过一辆车，车灯划破雨幕，又很快消失在转角。巷子里积起小小的水坑，映着零星的灯影，随雨点一圈圈晃动。空气里弥漫着潮湿泥土的气味，混着一丝凉意，钻进衣领。整座城市仿佛放慢了呼吸，只剩雨声填满寂静，像一首没有歌词的曲子，在黑夜里独自流淌。
